text:
**Short answer:** for most camping trips, get a compact 250-500Wh LiFePO4 unit. It's light enough to carry one-handed and covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP. Go bigger only if you need a fridge or electric cooler.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 290Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb, 300W). It's the top pick in [PowerStationGearLab's ranking](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/). Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so you'll find the Plus mainly through Amazon and other retailers.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh, 5-year warranty, built-in lantern). It's the cheapest of the group, per the same guide. Make sure you get the standard AC-outlet version, not the "C300 DC."
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W inverter, expandable to 572Wh). It's the best pick if you want more output.
- **[BLUETTI Elite 30 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2)** ($289.99, or $275.50 with code AFF5OFF; 288Wh, 600W, 9.5 lb). Dealectric lists it as its light pick, and [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations) also recommends it. Its solar input maxes out at 28V, so many 100W+ folding panels won't work with it.

## Bigger setups (fridge, cooler, several days)
- **[BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** ($499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF; 1,152Wh, 1,800W, about 35 lb). It has no expansion port.
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (sale price under $530). [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) calls it the best value for most people, though its fan is noisy.
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** (under $900 on sale, 39 lb). OutdoorGearLab names it the best for multi-day off-grid camping.
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** ($1,079 on sale). [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/) picked it for camping. It's IP65-rated and weighs about 40 lb.

## Caveats
- Reviewers disagree on the small units. OutdoorGearLab scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) low, behind the larger models. Their ratings favor bigger units, so the small ones are best if weight matters more than runtime.
- Most of these pages earn affiliate commissions, and Dealectric only covers a few brands. It says it has no Jackery, EcoFlow, or Anker in its records.
- I only have working purchase links for the Dealectric items. For the Jackery, Anker, and EcoFlow models, search the exact model name on Amazon or the brand's site to confirm current prices.
- Turn off a CPAP's humidifier to stretch runtime to about 3-5 nights on a 288Wh unit.

If you tell me your gear (CPAP, fridge, laptop), trip length, and budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
